findings.problem: Pressing Enter in the first field the product ever offers does nothing at all. Driven on paper and on ink at 1440x960 and 390x844: click the field, type "3 October 2026", press Enter, and the harvested state is byte-identical before and after — hint still "For example, 3 October 2026.", aria-invalid still unset, heading still "When is the day?", no live-region announcement, no refusal. The same string committed by clicking "Set the day" replaces the screen with the count, writes "The day is set. Moments come next." and moves focus to "Add a moment". The field is a bare input with no <form> and no keydown listener; the delegated click handler at render-b.js:1596 is the only way in. The editor's own WHEN field DOES bind Enter (render-b.js:987-988, event.preventDefault + commitDate), so the surface teaches Enter as the commit key on the second screen and silently refuses it on the first. On a phone it is worse: with no form there is no "Go" key hint either, so the return key on the keyboard is simply inert. This is a single-field question put to someone who has never used a tool like this, and the universal reflex for answering it produces no motion, no error and no explanation.
findings.fix: Give the field the listener the editor's date field already carries. In the owner-empty branch, add to the h("input.b-input", { id: "b-empty-date", ... }) spec: on: { keydown: function (event) { if (event.key !== "Enter") return; event.preventDefault(); node.querySelector('[data-act="setday"]').click(); } }. The existing delegated handler then runs unchanged, so all three refusal sentences, the aria-invalid write, the screen replacement and the focus move to "Add a moment" are inherited exactly and nothing else moves.

findings.element: .b-seg button[aria-pressed="true"] — the "What guests see" Shown/Hidden pair in the editor (b.css:837)
findings.problem: The selected segment is drawn by fill alone — background: var(--fore); color: var(--back) — and a forced palette repaints exactly that. Measured in Chromium with forcedColors:"active" at 1440x960 on both grounds, editor open on Send the invitations: on paper Shown (aria-pressed=true) computes bg rgb(255,255,255) / fg rgb(0,0,0) and Hidden (false) computes bg rgba(255,255,255,0) / fg rgb(0,0,0) over the same Canvas; on ink both compute white text on black. Border-width is 0px on the pressed half and 0 0 0 1px on the other, which is the divider, not a state. A screenshot of the group in forced colours shows two identical capsules. A sighted high-contrast user editing a moment cannot see whether that moment is shown to their guests or hidden from them — the one control on the surface whose entire job is to report a state. aria-pressed still carries it to a screen reader, so the loss falls precisely on the reader the forced-colours block at b.css:1547 was written for, and this is the only stateful control that block omits; it already carries the lead tick's meaning in geometry for exactly this reason.
findings.fix: Carry the selection in geometry as well as fill, in the same trailing @media (forced-colors: active) block. Add above the block: .b-seg button { position: relative; }. Add inside the block: .b-seg button[aria-pressed="true"] { forced-color-adjust: none; background: Highlight; color: HighlightText; } and .b-seg button[aria-pressed="true"]::after { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 6px; right: 6px; bottom: 3px; height: 2px; background: currentColor; }. System colour keywords introduce no hue and the rules are scoped to forced colours, so nothing on either ground changes.

findings.element: .b-gapNote — the sentence under TODAY IS 16 JULY in the pinned column, at 1024+ (render-b.js:357-365 and render-b.js:1334-1361)
findings.problem: Two writers own this node and one of them ignores where the plan pane is. speak() names the nearest row at or below the pane's top edge and is bound ONLY to scroll events (window and .b-plan, render-b.js:1366-1368). relay() overwrites the same node with gapSentence(items[0]) on every repaint, unconditionally. So any edit that repaints without moving the pane's scrollTop leaves the readout describing the top of the plan until the owner happens to scroll. Reproduced on both grounds at 1024x800, 1280x900 and 1440x800/960: open the editor on Venue walk-through, the pane settles at scrollTop 997 and the note correctly reads "19 September · 65 days away"; press −1 and, with scrollTop still exactly 997 and 19 September still the first row under the pane's edge, the note becomes "Nothing is planned until 1 August." and stays wrong through five further presses; nudging the pane by one pixel restores the right sentence. The same revert appears in a +7 run at scrollTop 499 and 751. The reverted sentence describes a stretch of plan roughly a thousand pixels above the fold — the case the surface's own rule ("goes back to the gap when the gap is on screen") forbids — and it fires on the owner's most frequent action, one line beneath the 79-day figure it is meant to qualify.
findings.fix: Make the repaint use the scroll-aware writer instead of a second, blinder one. In wireOwner, immediately after the definition of speak, add: root.__gapSpeak = speak;. Then in relay(), after the existing note.textContent = items.length ? ... : "Nothing is planned yet."; write, add: var f = measureEl.closest(".b-field"); if (f && f.__gapSpeak) f.__gapSpeak();. speak() already returns early when .b-stick is not position:sticky and derives every string live from gapSentence() and the rows' own data-date/data-away, so the phone, the tablet band and the empty-measure guard are untouched.

biggestWin: The keyboard model is complete and it holds under abuse. Twelve consecutive +7 presses at 1440 leave focus on the pressed stepper at a constant y=829 with scrollY pinned at 0, the readout tracking the absolute date, and the ceiling stating itself in words ("This is as far as it goes. Nothing can sit after the day itself.") rather than swallowing the press or disabling the control; Ctrl+Z walks back through the stack and hands focus back to the exact node that made each change; Escape returns focus to the precise row that opened the panel and still records the rename typed before it; delete lands focus on a neighbouring row rather than the body, and undo brings the moment, the field and the focus back together. At every desk width from 1024 to 1440, on both grounds, the pane re-scrolls itself so the row being edited is FULLY inside the plan pane after every single move — measured, not sampled. And the loading frame is the best-made thing here: at 390 its four skeletons sit at y65/h86, y161, y195, y230 and the arrived data lands at y65/h86, y163, y193, y228, with the today label at y280 in both — the promise and the arrival are the same composition, so nothing hops when the plan turns up.
